newsitem.title: UK: UK to allow some magazine-sponsored TV programmes.
newsitem.headline: UK to allow some magazine-sponsored TV programmes.

text.p: Britain's television watchdog on Wednesday said it would allow cable and satellite channels to broadcast "masthead" programmes, but will continue to ban that form of programme sponsorship on terrestrial channels.

Masthead programming refers to TV programmes made or funded by magazine or other print publishers, which incorporates the publication name in the programme title and has editorial content similar to the publication.

Britain's commercial, terrestrial television networks -- ITV, Channel 4 and the soon-to-be-launched Channel 5 -- will continue to be banned from broadcasting masthead programmes, the Independent Television Commission (ITC) said in its new code on programme sponsorship.
The new code opening masthead programming to cable and satellite channels will be reviewed after one year, the ITC said.

Other revisions to the ITC code on programme sponsorship include greater scope for sponsorship of "how to do" programmes, greater scope for the use of straplines, and an increase on game shows in the number of brand references to prizes permitted to two from one, the ITC said.
Instructional, or "how to do", programmes may now be sponsored by advertisers who supply products or services relevant to the programme's field of interest, the ITC said.
Also under the revised code, programme credits may include audio and/or visual straplines that clearly refer to the programme itself or to the sponsor's relationship to the programme, the ITC said.
